task_title: Allow net-win incumbent flips in AI Sweep Eval promotion gate

plan_review.notes: Verdict: approved_with_changes, no re-architecture warranted. Alt considered: pass incumbent stats as a separate parameter to selectQualifiedWinner instead of eager per-row field -- rejected because 2 of 3 call sites (round-plan.ts, sweep-eval.ts) prefilter out the incumbent row before calling the gate, so eager computation during buildLeaderboard (where incumbent rows are still in scope) is required; a lazy/parameterized approach would need those two callers to separately thread incumbent totals through, more invasive for no benefit. Concerns addressed: (1) documented the single-incumbent-per-buildLeaderboard-call invariant in BuildLeaderboardOptions doc comment + added a regression test scoping incumbent identity to (combo,configId) not configId alone; (2) clarified sortByLexicographic doc comment as diagnostic-only (not a gate) since flipsVsIncumbent is still used there as a display tie-break; (3) added a superseded-notice to the 2026-07-19 handoff so operators do not apply the old zero-flip rule from stale docs; (4) confirmed no float-creep risk in winsVsIncumbentDelta (integer .length-derived counts only).

rounds.notes: Native GitHub Copilot PR reviewer left 4 inline comments on PR #1735 after CI went green: (1) winsVsIncumbentDelta was computed from raw win counts without verifying candidate/incumbent ran an identical (weapon,seed) panel, which could bias the gate if coverage ever diverges from the intended full panel; (2) the decrease-rejection regression test didn't isolate the decrease clause from the 90%-floor clause; (3) a broken markdown paragraph in the handoff doc; (4) a test comment inaccurately claimed a fixture 'recovers nothing else' when it also recovers seed 10. All 4 were fixed concurrently by two actors: an automated copilot-swe-agent[bot] push (commit 6b72ddf2) landed a samePanel Set-equality guard on winsVsIncumbentDelta in aggregate-shards.ts (the only field the hard gate reads), fixed the handoff markdown, redesigned the decrease-test with a 10-seed same-panel fixture, added a new 'rejects a candidate evaluated on a different weapon/seed panel' regression test, and fixed the comment inaccuracy plus 2 sweep-eval-search-promotion.test.ts tests broken by the new panel check. This session independently diagnosed and fixed the same 4 findings in parallel; after a push-rejection surfaced the bot's concurrent commit, this session reset to the bot's tip (avoiding duplicate/conflicting logic) and finished the 3 sweep-round-plan.test.ts tests the bot's fix did not touch, redesigning their fixtures so candidate and incumbent share an identical (weapon,seed) panel. Deliberately did not extend the samePanel guard to flipsVsIncumbent/winRateDeltaVsIncumbent beyond the bot's scope: those two fields are diagnostic/tie-break-only (sortByLexicographic, leaderboard markdown) and are never read by the hard qualification gate, so guarding only winsVsIncumbentDelta closes the actual gate-bypass vector without unnecessary divergence from the already-landed fix. Verified: 299/299 tests/unit/ai pass, tsc --noEmit clean, verify:fast green.

A follow-up native GitHub Copilot PR review pass on this session's round-2 push (commit f066ec82) left 4 more inline comments, all pointing at test fixtures where a candidate added an extra (weapon, seed) cell not present in the incumbent's panel, so winsVsIncumbentDelta would be null (panel mismatch) and the candidate would be disqualified for the wrong reason rather than exercising the intended code path. Investigation showed 2 of the 4 were stale: GitHub's line-remap landed old comments (from before this session's round-plan.ts fixes) onto already-correct lines that matched the reviewer's own recommended pattern. The other 2 were genuine: (a) 'does NOT promote an improving candidate when the round is partial' (sweep-round-plan.test.ts) had a 2-cell incumbent baseline vs. a 3-cell candidate shard -- fixed by adding the third cell (dagger/3) to the incumbent as a loss, keeping panels identical while giving the candidate a genuine 3-vs-2 win-count edge (also updated the resulting bestScore/rows-length assertions); (b) 'returns null when the only qualifying candidate does not out-score the current position' (sweep-eval-search-promotion.test.ts) had a candidate with an extra bow/1 cell absent from the incumbent's 10-seed sword-only panel -- fixed by adding that bow/1 cell to the incumbent as a loss so the candidate's 11-vs-10 win-count edge is real, not panel-mismatch noise. Verified: 299/299 tests/unit/ai pass, tsc --noEmit clean, verify:fast green.

A final native GitHub Copilot PR review pass on commit 9aefd6a identified a genuine logic gap in sweep-eval.ts's legacy --stage search path: selectSearchPromotion was called with comboStr as incumbentCombo even for non-LEGACY combos (e.g. navmesh+legacy), making buildLeaderboard unable to find the LEGACY incumbent rows (tagged legacy+legacy) and forcing winsVsIncumbentDelta to null, which disqualified every candidate. The fix mirrors initCheckpoint in round-plan.ts: (1) added optional incumbentCombo? parameter to selectSearchPromotion defaulting to comboStr for backward compatibility; (2) added optional legacyBaseline? to searchCombo opts; (3) when combo !== legacy+legacy and legacyBaseline is provided, extract LEGACY config ID, inject rows + configs into allRows/configs, set incumbentConfigId/incumbentCombo to the LEGACY values, and pass incumbentCombo to selectSearchPromotion; (4) added --legacy-baseline CLI flag to --stage search; (5) added 2 regression tests covering the non-LEGACY combo path (passes with incumbentCombo, fails/disqualifies without it). Verified: 104/104 tests/unit/ai pass, tsc --noEmit clean, verify:fast green.

A further native GitHub Copilot PR review pass on the round-4 push found that fix's --legacy-baseline flag was opt-in only: the default `--stage search` invocation (no flag) silently preserved the original bug (gating a non-LEGACY combo against its own baseline instead of the fixed LEGACY incumbent). An automated copilot-swe-agent[bot] push (commit a4a5bb57) landed a fix matching that exact opt-in design (flag present -> correct behavior; flag omitted -> old buggy default silently preserved). This session judged that insufficient against the reviewer's intent and the task's 'share the same rule' requirement, and strengthened it on top of the bot's commit: when opts.legacyBaseline is NOT supplied, searchCombo now automatically computes the LEGACY baseline inline (one extra headless eval pass reusing register()/buildTasks()/runTasks(), mirroring the existing evalStandalone/validate pattern), so correctness no longer depends on remembering to pass a flag. --legacy-baseline is now purely a perf optimization to reuse a precomputed LEGACY shard across multiple combo searches, never a correctness requirement. Verified: 46/46 (targeted) + 301/301 (tests/unit/ai) pass, tsc --noEmit clean, eslint clean, verify:fast green.

A further native GitHub Copilot PR review pass on the round-5 push found the --legacy-baseline artifact was JSON.parse'd and its rows injected into allRows/configs with zero provenance or row validation: a stale/wrong-floor/wrong-budget/pre-v2-schema artifact (missing safeRoomMs) could silently corrupt the incumbent's win count, and the freshly-stamped output metadata would hide this from the downstream --stage validate check. Fixed by adding assertLegacyBaselineProvenance() in sweep-eval.ts, which: (1) validates the artifact has exactly one config; (2) validates every row is tagged combo === LEGACY_COMBO_ID; (3) reuses the existing assertSearchArtifactProvenance() to check schema version, stage, floorId, budgetMs, and maxFrames against the current runner's calibration; (4) reuses the newly-exported assertRowSafeRoomInRange() (aggregate-shards.ts) on every row to reject missing/out-of-range safeRoomMs. searchCombo's `if (opts.legacyBaseline)` branch now calls this single validator instead of an ad-hoc inline config-count check. Added 8 new regression tests (tests/unit/ai/sweep-eval-search-promotion.test.ts): accepts a well-formed artifact; rejects >1 config; rejects mixed/wrong combo tags; rejects stale schemaVersion, floorId mismatch, budgetMs mismatch, maxFrames mismatch; rejects a row missing safeRoomMs. Verified: 15/15 (targeted) + 309/309 (tests/unit/ai) pass, tsc --noEmit clean, eslint clean, verify:fast green.

Native GitHub Copilot PR review flagged the PR description itself as stale relative to the committed review ledger and handoff: it reported 101 targeted tests and a single clean code-review round with zero concerns, while the durable records showed 119 (later corrected to 112) targeted tests and 6 rounds with 11 resolved concerns. Fixed by rewriting the PR description via the GitHub API to match the ledger/handoff exactly. No code change; docs/process-only finding.

Native GitHub Copilot PR review found .github/workflows/ai-sweep.yml checkpoint-init job comments still called the safety gate a flip check that rejects any candidate which flips LEGACY wins -- the superseded zero-flip wording. An automated copilot-swe-agent[bot] push (commit b8e97f2b) fixed the wording to describe the net-win comparison actually enforced (>=90% wins AND strictly more total wins than incumbent); this session independently authored an equivalent fix, found the bots adequate, and reset to the bots commit rather than duplicate it. Also caught and fixed (via bot commit dabe0e82) a stale test-count arithmetic error in the handoff (46 claimed vs 39 actual for sweep-round-plan.test.ts, corrected total 119->112); the PR description was updated to match. No production code change; docs/comment-only findings.
